short: Bundled phonetic-feature streams (M06) are ahead of 2009 EMG recognizers, but tuning on the test set inflates the gain; the speaker-independent and silent-speech claims are untested.
position: The paper [@schultz2010modeling] changes the EMG acoustic model (M06): nine phonetic-feature streams whose models are bundled by decision trees, beside a phone stream. The design is ahead: none of the 12 prior non-acoustic-signal recognizers bundles features (Appendix), the group's feature streams [@jou2007continuous] and clustered triphones [@wand2009towards] were separate, and the gain holds over 28 sessions of 14 speakers and under pooled training. Its size is an upper bound, because stream weights and tree size were tuned on the test set (§3.3). The "speaker-independent" result (M03) tests the speakers it trained on (§4), weaker than the group's earlier held-out-speaker design on the same corpus [@wand2009towards]. Usefulness for silent speech rests on audible scores only; the group's [concurrent] silent test with the same features gave above 80% WER for most speakers [@wand2009impact].
